title: Battalion-and-below DDIL-native orders, planning and battle-tracking app bridging dismounted TAK and Onebrief-class HQ planning (structured orders, reports and tracking that survive displaced, low-bandwidth command posts)
problem: Between the dismounted TAK client and the division-level planning suite, company and battalion staffs still run orders, reports and battle tracking on voice, MMC/TAK chat, PowerPoint and paper in displaced, low-bandwidth command posts, and neither TAK (no structured orders/planning objects) nor Onebrief-class tools (HQ collaboration design center, offline tactical mode still 'in development') natively covers that echelon under DDIL.

user.exact_role: Battalion S3/S2/S4 staff officers and battle captains/battle NCOs in the TOC or mobile command post; company commanders, XOs and 1SGs on Nett Warrior/ATAK end-user devices; SOF team leaders
user.echelon: Company through battalion (brigade as the consumer of reports and the source of orders)
organization_examples: 4th Infantry Division and 25th Infantry Division NGC2/TiC formations
IBCT infantry battalions (Infantry Magazine mobile-CP authors, Winter 2024-25)
Allied light forces (Bundeswehr Jaeger battalions, TNI-AD infantry battalions) and public-safety incident-command TAK users

current_workflow: 1. Receive higher's OPORD/FRAGO as a PDF/PowerPoint or a WinTAK data package over an intermittent ITN/MMC-T link, or by courier when the network is down.
2. Build the battalion/company order and graphics in PowerPoint, Word and on a paper map board; hand-draw or re-digitize graphics into WinTAK/ATAK as CoT overlays and data packages.
3. Disseminate the order by voice on TSM/PRC-163 nets, by MMC/TAK chat, and by physically pushing data packages to leaders' end-user devices.

4. Track combat power, LOGSTAT, PERSTAT, SITREP and SPOTREP by voice and free-text chat; a battle NCO re-keys them into an Excel/PowerPoint battle-tracking chart and a paper 'analog' COP for when the digital picture dies.
5. Re-brief higher by phone, chat or a slide deck; when the CP jumps or the link drops, the running estimate and report history are lost or diverge between nodes and are reconciled by hand afterward.
current_solution: Voice (TSM/PRC-163), MMC/JBC-P (ATAK-based MMC-S) for chat and PLI, WinTAK/ATAK for graphics and COP, PowerPoint/Excel/paper for orders and battle tracking; in NGC2 prototype divisions, the Anduril-led baseline (Lattice UI, Palantir data layer, Onebrief as the planning layer) claims DDIL data exchange and squadron-level battle tracking when cut off from the division cloud; SBMC (Anduril/Rivet) will supply a company-and-below C2 client that must be backward compatible with ATAK; allied forces use Systematic SitaWare Edge/Frontline (with a tasking function) or Ukraine's Delta (works offline).
failure: Structured content (orders, tasks, reports, running estimates) has no native object model in TAK, so it travels as chat text, slides and data packages that do not merge when nodes reconnect after a displacement; Onebrief's structured planning objects live at division/corps with an offline tactical mode still 'in development' (company statement); the result is manual re-keying at the battalion TOC, divergent pictures between the main CP, the mobile CP and companies, and reports that are lost when the CP jumps.

evidence.claim: Infantry Magazine authors state IBCT command posts have lost the art of mobility, survivability and minimal connectivity while keeping a COP, and describe the battalion-and-below stack as voice over TSM/PRC-163, graphics/COP over WinTAK and chat/PLI over MMC - i.e., no structured orders/reports layer below brigade.
evidence.source_title: Utilizing the Integrated Tactical Network in Mobile Command Posts (Infantry Magazine, Winter 2024-2025; reprinted RealClearDefense 2025-03-01)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army's SBMC Request for Solutions (SAM.gov, April 2025) defines SBMC as the future situational awareness and mission command platform for company level and below dismounted operations and requires backward compatibility with the ATAK architecture - the dismounted C2 client will remain TAK-shaped through at least FY2028.
evidence.source_title: Soldier Borne Mission Command (SBMC) Other Transaction Opportunity (SAM.gov)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: SBMC prototype agreements: Anduril $159M and Rivet $195M (Sept 2025, 18-month sprints; prototype awards, not production); Anduril reported moving from phase one to phase two in Aug 2026 after testing with the 75th Ranger Regiment.
evidence.source_title: Army awards more than $350M in contracts for Soldier Borne Mission Command system prototypes; Anduril redesigns tech for Army's SBMC program (DefenseScoop)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: PM Mission Command 'Operational Mission Command Suite' notice requires the TAK solution to support on-prem, hybrid and cloud data services integrated via DDIL-robust protocols and architectures (from earlier-stage evidence E02-F8; SAM.gov primary page blocked this session).
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO-26-108019 quotes a soldier who tested NGC2 'in a denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited environment where we were essentially cut off from the division's cloud, but we were still able to battle track and execute our tasks at the squadron level internally'; Army says the NGC2 baseline provides real-time data exchange in DDIL. This is evidence the incumbent NGC2 stack already addresses part of this gap at battalion-equivalent echelon (weakens the gap), while the Army still lacks a unit-by-year schedule and life-cycle cost estimate.
evidence.source_title: GAO-26-108019 Army Modernization: Better Schedule and Cost Information Needed to Support Scaling Battlefield Network
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Onebrief states that 'development of fully offline access for tactical units in austere environments is underway' and that planners used it 'inside displaced, low-bandwidth command posts' during Ivy Sting - a company claim that the offline tactical mode is not yet shipped and that its results are self-reported (no independent measurement found).
evidence.source_title: Onebrief Compresses Army Planning Timelines from Hours to Minutes as NGC2 Scales to a Full Division (Business Wire press release)
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: Ivy Sting 4 (early 2026) deliberately tested C2 of maneuver from division to battalion under denied network conditions - DDIL C2 at battalion is an explicit Army test objective, not an edge case.
evidence.source_title: 4th Infantry Division Leads NGC2 Prototyping with Ivy Sting 4 (CPE C2IN LinkedIn post)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Practitioner critique (former Army officer) that vendors treat DDIL as an edge case; 25th ID's 'first mile, last mile' focus (LinkedIn post; RECALL from earlier stage - not re-verified this session).
evidence.source_title: Tom Keane LinkedIn post on Ivy Sting 5 / 'own the edge'
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The TAK community keeps building low-bandwidth transports and offline map tooling (Akita-MeshTAK for Meshtastic/Reticulum; takwerx map-depot), and no TAK Product Center plugin for structured operations orders or mission planning was found in this session's search - demand for DDIL operation exists but the orders/planning object layer is missing from the open ecosystem.
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: Allied/foreign incumbents already ship partial answers: Systematic added a tasking function to SitaWare Frontline and SitaWare Edge so units 'plan and follow missions in real time' over its low-bandwidth STC protocol; Ukraine's Delta 'can work offline' and at least one NATO country explored adopting it (April 2025). Shows the feature is buildable and that the allied market has entrenched vendors.
evidence.source_title: SitaWare Edge: Situational Awareness for Dismounted Commanders (Systematic product page); Delta (situational awareness system) (Wikipedia)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Immersive Wisdom holds a DoD-wide five-year sole-source ordering contract (ceiling $25M through GFY2029, awarded by the USAF) for TRL-9 no-/low-bandwidth collaboration software, plus an AFWERX STRATFI with three DoD commands - a paying buyer exists for the DDIL collaboration primitive (ceiling is not revenue; obligations unknown).
evidence.source_title: SOF Week 2024: Immersive Wisdom awarded DoD-wide five-year sole-source $25MM ordering contract (PR Newswire)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Onebrief received an Army Contracting Command enterprise IDIQ (W9128Z-26-D-A014, $20M ceiling, Sept 2026) usable by any DoD warranted contracting officer - the HQ planning layer is now on an enterprise vehicle, so the incumbent can be ordered at any echelon once its offline mode ships (ceiling, not revenue).
evidence.source_title: Onebrief enterprise contract press release (Business Wire, 2026-09-17) and B02 company record
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: III Armored Corps is receiving baseline NGC2 capabilities (Sept 2026), i.e., the Anduril/Palantir/Onebrief baseline is spreading beyond the two prototype divisions before any third-party battalion orders app exists.
evidence.source_title: III Armored Corps receiving baseline NGC2 capabilities (DefenseScoop)
evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: The echelon has no program office of its own: dismounted C2 belongs to PEO Soldier (Nett Warrior/SBMC, now with Anduril and Rivet owning the UI), the TOC belongs to CPE C2IN (NGC2 baseline led by Anduril with Onebrief as the planning layer), and TAK itself is government-owned with TAK-MIL distribution controlled by the TAK Product Center, so a battalion orders app has no natural buyer or budget line and must ride as a plugin or a team-member subcontract. Venture-backed entrants (Onebrief, Anduril) went to the division/corps and program-of-record money first and are now moving down-echelon; DDIL-consistent sync (CRDT/merge of orders, graphics and reports across nodes that reconnect out of order) is technically demanding and unglamorous; unit-level budgets are GPC-card sized; and allied markets are held by Systematic (NATO standard) and national systems, so no startup has found an economic wedge at this echelon.
technical_wedge: A DDIL-native 'orders and reports object layer' for battalion and below: an ATAK/WinTAK plugin plus lightweight TAK Server-side service that represents OPORD/FRAGO, tasks, control measures, sync matrix and standard reports (SITREP, LOGSTAT, PERSTAT, SPOTREP, 9-line) as structured, versioned objects synchronized with a CRDT/merge model over any TAK transport (TSM, MANET, Meshtastic/goTenna-class mesh, SATCOM) so that displaced nodes reconcile without re-keying; it imports higher's products (Onebrief export, PDF/PPT parsing) and emits CoT/data packages downward and structured reports upward, and can later map to the NGC2 common data baseline and Lattice SDK. The startup competes on the merge model, the small-screen orders UX and the open TAK footprint, not on the map or the transport.

mvp.what: ATAK-CIV plugin + companion web client + open TAK Server extension implementing structured orders/tasks/reports with offline-first, conflict-free sync and a 'CP jump' recovery mode; unclassified, built on public doctrine formats (FM 6-0 order/report templates).
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Three to five Android EUDs and one laptop 'TOC' on a Meshtastic/goTenna-class mesh with deliberate partitions: issue an order, task subordinates, submit reports while disconnected, jump the TOC, reconnect out of order and show every node converging on the same order version and report log with no manual reconciliation; benchmark bytes-per-order and convergence time against sending the same content as chat and data packages.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That structured orders/reports (not just PLI and chat) can be authored, disseminated and reconciled at kilobit-class bandwidth with partition tolerance; that battle captains and company XOs prefer it to chat + PowerPoint in a field exercise (measured re-keying time and report loss); and that it installs and runs within the TAK plugin process without TPC-controlled binaries.

data_requirement.what: Unclassified doctrinal formats for orders and reports (FM 6-0, ATP 6-0.5, unit SOPs and TACSOP report formats), CoT/TAK data-package schemas, sample graphics (MIL-STD-2525 symbology), and realistic network-partition traces; no operational or classified data needed for MVP.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Yes for the MVP: doctrine and symbology are public; ATAK-CIV and the TAK SDK are open source; unit TACSOPs can be obtained from National Guard or allied units under CRADA/exercise participation. Real unit report data and NGC2 data-baseline schemas require a government sponsor or team-lead partnership and may be CUI.
sources: Army Publishing Directorate (FM 6-0 Commander and Staff Organization and Operations; ATP 6-0.5 Command Post Organization and Operations)

NGC2 common data baseline / Anduril Lattice SDK and Palantir data layer (later)

Lattice SDK (partner program) and NGC2 data-baseline APIs from Operation Jailbreak (access unverified)

budget.program_or_line: NGC2 C2 Applications (FY2026 request ~$488.4M RDT&E per buyer map; PE not verified) and the SBMC prototype agreements ($159M Anduril + $195M Rivet, prototype not production); no dedicated line for a battalion orders app exists.
budget.evidence: GAO-26-108019: ~$3.3B identified for NGC2 through FY2026 in PB2026 documentation, no life-cycle cost estimate or unit-by-year schedule; SBMC production decision reported for FY2028 (CRS IF13022, July 2026). A startup would be paid from a team-lead subcontract, a SBIR/xTech award or unit-level GPC/OTA money, not from a named line.

entry_vehicle.primary: TAK plugin published through TAK.gov (ATAK-CIV first, then TAK-GOV review) plus an Army xTech/SBIR Direct-to-Phase-II or AAL problem-set award, with an allied/public-safety paying pilot in parallel
sequence: 1. Open-source ATAK-CIV plugin + TAK Server extension; field test with a National Guard battalion, public-safety incident-command TAK users or a German/Indonesian light unit on unclassified networks (CRADA/no-cost)
2. xTechSearch/xTechIgnite or Army SBIR Phase I/D2P2 (eligibility contingent on ownership rules) or Bundeswehr Cyber Innovation Hub / NATO DIANA pilot for the allied path
3. Team-member subcontract under an NGC2 team lead (Anduril or Lockheed) or Lattice partner-program onboarding as the 'orders/reports' app; SBMC ecosystem via ATAK compatibility
4. Enterprise ordering via an existing vehicle (Onebrief-style Army IDIQ, or a SBIR Phase III) once a unit sponsor exists
entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% ownership by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (and the xTech-linked SBIR route inherits this); with one founder not assumed to be a U.S. person, the cap table must be structured so U.S.-person owners hold the majority, or the SBIR path is unavailable - needs counsel. TAK-GOV/MIL access and plugin signing require a U.S. government sponsor; ATAK-CIV is open. Allied entry (Bundeswehr CIHBw, NATO DIANA) may be easier for a German founder but does not lead to U.S. Army budget.

competition.how_close: Very close from above: NGC2 planning layer at 4th ID, Army enterprise IDIQ (Sept 2026), $2.15B valuation; states fully offline access for tactical units is 'underway'.
Very close from below: SBMC prototype UI owners for company-and-below; Lattice is the NGC2 baseline UI; both must be ATAK-backward-compatible.

competition.company: TAK Product Center / PM Mission Command (government)
competition.how_close: Owns ATAK/WinTAK/TAK Server and MMC-S; could add structured orders natively; Operational Mission Command Suite notice already asks for DDIL-robust TAK data services.
Close in allied markets: tasking function to plan and follow missions in real time over its STC low-bandwidth protocol; NATO standard HQ system.
Adjacent: ultra-low-bandwidth collaborative war room on SIPR for SOF/AOC, not TAK-native structured orders.
competition.evidence: PR Newswire 2024-05 sole-source $25M ordering contract; E03-F29

competition.how_close: Proof that an offline-capable, unit-built situational-awareness/tasking app can be fielded nationally; not a U.S. competitor but an allied-market alternative.

competition.company: PAR Government, Booz Allen, Cloud-RF, Lyntris/Accelint, goTenna/Somewear (Forterra)
competition.how_close: TAK plugin/services vendors and mesh transports; partial pieces (transport, RF planning, plugins-as-services) but no structured orders layer found.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily: Anduril already owns the SBMC and Lattice UIs and the NGC2 baseline lead; Onebrief has publicly committed to offline tactical access; the TAK Product Center could add order objects to ATAK/WinTAK; Systematic already has a tasking function. Any of them can ship a 'good enough' battalion orders feature within one prototype cycle.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only if it treats this as an open, transport-agnostic TAK-native layer that incumbents do not prioritize (they optimize for their own stacks), proves a measurably better partition-tolerant merge model, and sells first where incumbents are absent (National Guard, public safety, allied light forces), then enters the NGC2/SBMC ecosystems as a partner app. Honest assessment: as a standalone U.S. Army venture the wedge is likely to be absorbed; it is more credible as a feature company that gets acquired or as a partner-program app, or as an allied-first product.

capital_required.proof_of_concept_usd: $150k-$300k (two founders + one contract Android/TAK engineer, 6 months, commercial EUDs and mesh radios)
capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: $1M-$2.5M (12-18 months: TAK-GOV review, security hardening, a field exercise with a Guard or allied battalion, an SBIR D2P2 or xTech award, one ex-battalion S3 on staff)
capital_required.first_production_deployment_usd: $5M-$12M (ATO/RMF or riding an NGC2 team lead's authorization, TAK-MIL packaging, CMMC, sustained field support for one division or an allied brigade; assumes subcontract or SBIR Phase III rather than a program of record)
capital_required.assumptions: Software-only, unclassified through demo; no hardware; heavy dependence on a government sponsor for TAK-GOV/MIL access; SBIR only if ownership structure qualifies; figures are analyst estimates (HYPOTHESIS, LOW confidence).

expertise_required.role: Former battalion S3/XO or battle captain (recent TiC/CTC experience) as product lead or co-founder
expertise_required.why: Defines the order/report object model, SOP variance and TOC workflow; opens unit-level pilots; credibility with PM MC and TPC.

expertise_required.role: Distributed-systems engineer with CRDT/offline-first sync and Android (ATAK SDK) experience
expertise_required.why: Partition-tolerant merge of orders/graphics/reports across intermittent mesh links is the core technical claim.

expertise_required.role: TAK ecosystem engineer (TAK Server, CoT, data packages, TAK.gov plugin submission)
expertise_required.why: Distribution and interoperability with ATAK/WinTAK/MMC-S; navigating TPC review.
Bandwidth budgeting and realistic partition testing; can be contract or advisor.

expertise_required.role: Government BD / contracts advisor (SBIR eligibility, OTA team-member subcontracts, ATO)
expertise_required.why: Finding the buyer in a fragmented echelon and structuring the cap table for SBIR.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Unclassified, software-only C2 tooling built on open-source ATAK-CIV can be developed without licenses; but TAK-GOV/MIL access and plugin signing are government-controlled, deployment on Army networks requires RMF/ATO (or riding a team lead's authorization), CMMC applies once CUI flows, and a military-specific C2 application may be ITAR-controlled (USML Category XI/XXI) or EAR-controlled depending on design - requires export-control counsel before sharing code with the non-U.S.-person founder or allied units.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: If the Indonesian founder is not a U.S. person, giving them access to ITAR-controlled technical data or TAK-GOV/MIL software could be a deemed export; SBIR ownership rules and FOCI considerations for any facility clearance also apply. Mitigations (keeping the codebase EAR99/commercial, using ATAK-CIV only, separating controlled work) need counsel - no legal judgment made here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Public-safety incident command (wildland fire, SAR, disaster response) already uses TAK and suffers the same offline structured-tasking gap (ICS forms), and mining/energy/expedition operations need offline tasking; but the military-specific orders/reports model is the core value and commercial demand for partition-tolerant tasking is niche.

defensibility.explanation: Defensibility is weak: the merge/sync algorithms are replicable, ATAK is open, and incumbents own the surrounding UIs. What can compound is the installed base in units and allied forces, TAK.gov-approved status, integrations with Onebrief/Lattice/NGC2 data baseline, and a validated orders/report object schema units adopt in their SOPs.

why_now: Transformation in Contact and NGC2 put weekly vendor-unit iteration and DDIL testing at battalion level (Ivy Sting 4, early 2026); SBMC/Nett Warrior will put an ATAK-compatible C2 client on every leader by ~FY2028; the Army opened APIs through Operation Jailbreak (May 2026) and declared an NGC2 common data baseline (June 2026); ATAK-CIV and its SDK are open source; cheap mesh radios (Meshtastic/goTenna) and mature CRDT libraries make offline-first sync buildable by a small team; and the Ukraine war normalized unit-built, offline-capable C2 apps (Delta).
killer_risk: The gap is being closed from both sides by funded incumbents before a startup can reach a buyer: Onebrief states offline tactical access is in development and now holds an Army enterprise IDIQ, Anduril/Rivet own the SBMC dismounted UI (ATAK-compatible) and Anduril leads the NGC2 baseline that GAO already quotes as enabling squadron-level battle tracking when cut off from the division cloud; there is no program office or budget line for a battalion orders app, so the most likely outcome is a feature absorbed into Lattice, Onebrief or ATAK itself.

allied_extension: More compelling for entry, less for scale: allied light forces (Bundeswehr, Nordic, Baltic, Indonesian and Philippine units) and NATO partners already use ATAK or SitaWare Edge and face the same low-bandwidth orders problem, and a German founder can use Bundeswehr CIHBw/NATO DIANA channels without U.S.-person constraints; but Systematic is the NATO standard with its own tasking function, Ukraine's Delta is a free-of-charge national alternative attracting NATO interest, and allied budgets at this echelon are small, so allies improve pilot access and dual-track credibility rather than the total market.
